reason: Two searches (North Ridge trip reports; north ridge 5.6 via Cliff/Bluff Lake). Every Chaval result covered the West Route, the west face or the west ridge, mostly on SummitPost and CascadeClimbers (403) or in a WTA trip report (403). No reachable page describes a North Ridge on Mount Chaval, so its grade, pitches and timing cannot be confirmed.

One search and one opened source (Steph Abegg, Mystery Ridge enchainment). It confirms the ridge as a descent from Crowder's summit to a heather camp at Pickell Pass (third-class ledges, some fourth-class moves, a rappel near the base, a chasm splitting the lower ridge). But it gives only a whole-day total for a multi-peak traverse day, with no figures for this ridge. Every other result was a CascadeClimbers report (403). One source, and that one describing a traverse, is not enough for a stand-alone plan.

itinerary.cal: A summer route. The La Bohn Gap slope can hold hard snow into July, when crampons and an axe are worth carrying. Alpine Lakes Wilderness rules apply, including a free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead.
itinerary.totalNote: Usually done as one very long day of roughly 25 miles and 7,000 ft round trip, or split by camping in Necklace Valley or at the La Bohn Lakes. No opened source states a time for the round trip.

days.title: Necklace Valley to La Bohn Gap and the summit
days.objective: Reach Hinman's summit from La Bohn Gap and return to the car
days.note: Follow the East Fork Foss trail and the steep, rooty climb into Necklace Valley. The trail fades near the head of the valley, and the way continues off trail to the La Bohn Lakes and up to La Bohn Gap. From the gap, climb talus and broad open slopes (class 2) onto the ridge and follow it east to the top, crossing the upper edges of the shrinking north-side glaciers. The true high point lies a little further along the summit ridge than the first top you reach. Reverse the line to descend. Parties who want two days camp in Necklace Valley or at the La Bohn Lakes.

schedule.label: Necklace Valley
schedule.detail: Steep, rooty climb from the East Fork Foss into the valley.

schedule.label: La Bohn Lakes and La Bohn Gap
schedule.detail: Off trail from the head of the valley.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 2 talus and ridge from the gap; the true top is a little further along the ridge.

figureSources: Miles (about 25) and gain (about 7,000 ft) are the round-trip estimate from climberkyle's single-day ascent via the East Fork Foss and La Bohn. The class 2 line from the gap comes from climberkyle and from the guidebook text quoted on the karpoff page (talus east from La Bohn Gap to the ridge, then east to the summit). The Necklace Valley camp option is from karpoff. The turns-all-year report (Middle Fork approach) was used only to confirm that La Bohn Gap is misplaced on many maps. Hours are null because no opened source states a round-trip time for this approach.
rowIssues: The row says the climb heads due north from La Bohn Gap. The guidebook text quoted on the karpoff page sends it about half a mile east up talus (keeping left of the broad west ridge) and then east to the summit. Two opened sources also say the 'La Bohn Gap' label on USGS and other maps is in the wrong place, so a waypoint taken from the map label would be wrong. The row has no season, grade or descent.

reason: One search and one opened source (an Alpine Institute NW Rib route profile). It names the NE Ridge of the summit pyramid (5.7) only as one of two ways to finish from the Upper Curtis Glacier after the NW Rib, with no days, camps or times for it. Other results covered the Sulphide or Fisher Chimneys routes or were on 403 sites. The ridge is a finish to other climbs, not a trip of its own, and no second source describes it.

One search for the Northeast Ridge of Silver Star's west summit. Results confirm only its listing as Grade III 5.9 on SummitPost (403), plus trip reports for the Silver Star Glacier route via Burgundy Col (Mountaineers, 403). No reachable page describes the ridge's pitches, time on route or descent, so a plan would be the glacier route's plan with an invented ridge day.

One search. Only the Mountain Project area listing (5.7 M5-, mixed, one star) describes the route. No reachable page gives an approach time, a descent or a car-to-car figure, or anything beyond the shared New York Gully approach. One thin source is not enough.
One search for Spectre Peak's Haunted Wall returned nothing about the climb at all. No reachable source describes the route, and the row holds no waypoints or figures to check against.

One search, plus the Mountain Project area page opened. The area lists only Slippery Slab Tower's NE Face, and Thunder Mountain's documented route is the SE-slope scramble from Upper Thunder Lake. No reachable source describes a North Face route, so none of its figures can be sourced.
